item.text:
Using the supplied local prior as the structured base, and external sources only for ruler-specific narrative and institutional context. I did not score.

Bolsonaro’s office in 2022 was president of Brazil, the constitutionally defined head of the federal executive. He entered the year as an incumbent running for reelection, and his formal term ran through 31 December 2022. His core powers were the standard presidential ones in the 1988 Constitution, especially appointing and dismissing ministers, directing the federal administration, initiating legislation, issuing decrees, and vetoing bills. His main constraints in 2022 were also constitutional and institutional: Brazil’s direct two-round electoral system, the one immediate reelection limit, congressional permission requirements for long absences, and active judicial/electoral oversight from the TSE and STF.

The local prior already gives the main 2022 inherited conditions, so I did not re-fetch those structured datasets. In brief: Brazil in 2022 had low interstate/state-based conflict but nontrivial one-sided violence and repression, middling-to-weak governance and corruption indicators, and a mixed social/economic baseline with recovery from the pandemic but persistent food insecurity and institutional strain.

**Retained sources**
1. [Jair Messias Bolsonaro](https://www.biblioteca.presidencia.gov.br/presidencia/ex-presidentes/bolsonaro/Bolsonaro), Presidência da República library, undated current reference page. Precise fact: identifies Bolsonaro as president with `Período de Governo: 01/01/2019 a 31/12/2022`. Period fit: exact office span covering 2022. Ruler attribution: official government biography, useful as a favorable baseline. Limitations: it is biographical and celebratory, so it omits controversies. Contrary points: needs balancing with TSE/STF and independent reporting.

2. [Constituição da República Federativa do Brasil de 1988](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/constituicao/constituicaocompilado.htm?debug=true), Presidência da República / Planalto, current compiled constitutional text. Precise fact: articles 76, 77, and 84 establish that the president exercises the executive branch, is elected directly in a two-round system, and has enumerated powers over the federal administration. Period fit: governing law in force throughout 2022. Ruler attribution: legal framework, not ruler-specific. Limitations: tells you the rules, not how Bolsonaro used them. Contrary points: practice can diverge from formal powers.

3. [Lula e Bolsonaro vão disputar o 2º turno para a Presidência da República](https://www.tse.jus.br/comunicacao/noticias/2022/Outubro/lula-e-bolsonaro-vao-disputar-o-2o-turno-para-a-presidencia-da-republica), Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, 2 October 2022. Precise fact: Bolsonaro finished first round and advanced to the runoff. Period fit: exact 2022 election milestone. Ruler attribution: direct official election administration source. Limitations: reports vote totals, not campaign quality or legitimacy disputes. Contrary points: later fraud claims and protest dynamics are separate issues.

4. [TSE proclama eleitos presidente e vice-presidente da República Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e Geraldo Alckmin](https://www.tse.jus.br/comunicacao/noticias/2022/Dezembro/tse-proclama-eleitos-presidente-e-vice-presidente-da-republica-luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva-e-geraldo-alckmin), Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, 6 December 2022. Precise fact: formally proclaimed Lula and Alckmin elected after the second-round totalization. Period fit: closes Bolsonaro’s 2022 electoral arc. Ruler attribution: highest-value official election closure source. Limitations: formal result, not a narrative of post-election unrest. Contrary points: does not address the legitimacy claims made by Bolsonaro’s allies.

5. [Ministro Alexandre de Moraes autoriza compartilhamento de investigações envolvendo Bolsonaro](https://portal.stf.jus.br/noticias/verNoticiaDetalhe.asp?idConteudo=481714&ori=1), Supremo Tribunal Federal, 14 February 2022. Precise fact: STF reported investigative sharing involving Bolsonaro’s 2022 live that repeated fraud allegations about the voting system. Period fit: early-2022 institutional warning shot. Ruler attribution: official judiciary source, critical of false election claims. Limitations: it is a court notice, so it focuses on procedure, not broader governance. Contrary points: the note addresses alleged misconduct, not ordinary executive action.

6. [Bolsonaro chama embaixadores para atacar processo eleitoral; TSE rebate](https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2022/07/18/bolsonaro-chama-embaixadores-para-atacar-processo-eleitoral-com-afirmacoes-falsas.htm), Reuters via UOL Notícias, 18 July 2022. Precise fact: Bolsonaro summoned diplomats and repeated unsupported attacks on electronic voting; TSE publicly rebutted them. Period fit: major campaign-season confrontation with the electoral system. Ruler attribution: independent contemporaneous reporting. Limitations: it relays statements and reactions, not a full legal finding. Contrary points: supporters framed the event as scrutiny of the election system, not an attack on it.

7. [Analysis-Bolsonaro calls rallies to flex muscle on Brazil's bicentennial](https://www.euronews.com/2022/09/07/brazil-election-independence), Reuters via Euronews, 7 September 2022. Precise fact: Bolsonaro used Independence Day and bicentennial rallies to showcase support amid concerns about democratic institutions. Period fit: captures the political tone of the late-2022 campaign. Ruler attribution: independent reporting with institutional context. Limitations: analysis piece, so it is interpretive rather than purely documentary. Contrary points: it does not establish causation between rallies and later electoral outcomes.

8. [Bolsonaro volta a questionar urna eletrônica e diz que análise está sendo feita pelas Forças Armadas](https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2022/10/17/bolsonaro-volta-a-questionar-urna-eletronica-e-diz-que-analise-esta-sendo-feita-pelas-forcas-armadas.htm), Reuters via UOL Notícias, 17 October 2022. Precise fact: Bolsonaro again questioned electronic voting and pointed to military analysis of first-round voting. Period fit: shows the same institutional challenge persisting deep into the runoff period. Ruler attribution: independent, local-language reporting. Limitations: it reports claims; it does not validate them. Contrary points: TSE and election observers said the system was audit-ready and had no substantiated fraud evidence.

9. [Brazil's electoral court rejects Bolsonaro election challenge](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/brazils-electoral-court-rejects-bolsonaro-election-challenge-2951137), Reuters via Investing.com, 23 November 2022. Precise fact: Reuters reported the electoral court rejecting Bolsonaro allies’ challenge to the result. Period fit: central post-election institutional event. Ruler attribution: independent reporting on the formal dispute. Limitations: an aggregator host, so use the Reuters framing, not the site wrapper, as the real source. Contrary points: Bolsonaro supporters treated the challenge as a legitimate audit request, not a rejection of democracy.

10. [Brazil, Federative Republic of](https://ola.iaea.org/Applications/FactSheets/Country/Detail?code=BR), IAEA Office of Legal Affairs, current country fact sheet. Precise fact: Brazil is party to the key safeguards framework, including the bilateral Brazil-Argentina-IAEA safeguards agreement. Period fit: stable legal status relevant to 2022 nuclear posture. Ruler attribution: primary international legal source. Limitations: this is about legal status and safeguards, not domestic policy execution. Contrary points: it does not say anything about presidential control over nuclear policy.

11. [Brazil](https://pris.iaea.org/PRIS/CountryStatistics/CountryDetails.aspx?current=BR&mobile-app=true&theme=false), IAEA PRIS, current country profile. Precise fact: Brazil has two nuclear reactors in operation and one under construction, with the page also showing the 2022 nuclear electricity share trend. Period fit: useful capability context for Chapter 1B and nuclear-risk framing. Ruler attribution: primary operational nuclear source. Limitations: civil nuclear infrastructure only, not weapons intent or command authority. Contrary points: civil nuclear capacity should not be misread as evidence of nuclear weaponization.

12. [Food Insecurity and Food Inflation in Brazil](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/brazil/publication/brazil-food-insecurity-and-food-inflation), World Bank, 19 June 2023. Precise fact: the note states Brazil’s 2022 GDP grew 2.9 percent, labor-market recovery continued, but food insecurity and food-price pressures remained severe. Period fit: directly summarizes the inherited economic/social conditions entering and following 2022. Ruler attribution: neutral external context, not personal attribution. Limitations: published after 2022 and is diagnostic at the country level, not ruler-specific. Contrary points: some improvements in labor income and social transfers also appear in the note.

**Compact event map**
- 14 February 2022: STF action around Bolsonaro’s fraud allegations begins to be formally handled.
- 18 July 2022: Bolsonaro meets foreign diplomats and again attacks the voting system.
- 7 September 2022: Independence Day / bicentennial rallies become a display of strength and institutional confrontation.
- 2 October 2022: Bolsonaro reaches the runoff after the first round.
- 17 October 2022: Bolsonaro keeps questioning electronic voting and invokes military analysis.
- 30 October 2022: Bolsonaro loses the runoff.
- 23 November 2022: the post-election challenge is rejected.
- 6 December 2022: TSE formally proclaims Lula elected.
- 31 December 2022: Bolsonaro’s term ends.

**Chapter source plan**
- 1B: IAEA OLA + IAEA PRIS for Brazil’s civil nuclear baseline and safeguards status.
- 2B: local prior for conflict metrics, plus Reuters on institutional tension and election-period mobilization if narrative context is needed.
- 3B: local prior on repression and violence, plus STF July-February items and Reuters July/October for ruler attribution.
- 4B: Constitution + TSE + Reuters for elections, rights, and institutional constraint narrative.
- 5B: local GDP/income facts plus World Bank note for post-pandemic macro and food-security context.
- 6B: local health/education facts plus World Bank note for social stress context.
- 7B: local corruption/accountability priors plus Constitution and STF/Reuters for institutional conflict and anti-corruption or anti-disinformation framing.
- 8B: local governance-capacity priors plus Constitution and TSE for executive capacity and institutional limits.
